title: HyperEF 2.0: Spectral Hypergraph Coarsening via Krylov Subspace Expansion and Resistance-Based Local Clustering
problem: Hypergraph partitioning and coarsening require preserving structural properties while maintaining solution quality. Existing methods struggle to balance coarsening effectiveness with solution quality metrics like conductance.
motivation: Efficient, high-quality hypergraph partitioning is critical for VLSI physical design and circuit optimization at scale.
method: HyperEF 2.0 improves spectral coarsening through: (1) expanded Krylov subspace leveraging clique and star expansions for better effective resistance approximation, (2) resistance-based local clustering for balanced node merging, (3) integration into multilevel hypergraph partitioning with hyperedge weighting and community detection.
key_novelty: Krylov subspace-based spectral coarsening with resistance-based local clustering for improved balance.
contributions: Expanded Krylov subspace approach improving effective resistance approximation
Resistance-based local clustering for better cluster balance
State-of-the-art performance on VLSI hypergraph benchmarks
Up to 4.5× speedup over prior flow-based clustering methods
limitations: Evaluation limited to VLSI benchmarks; generalization to other hypergraph applications unclear.
primary_theme: Efficient spectral hypergraph partitioning for VLSI
